tagline: Wabash overlooks and a replica blockhouse tell different chapters of preservation.
intro: South and North River Roads in West Lafayette connect the journey to Wabash riverfront parks. Fort Ouiatenon has riverfront picnic grounds, while Tecumseh Trails Park overlooks the Wabash from North River Road. At Ross Hills, trails and a deck overlook accompany the picnic areas.

The river’s trading history predates these parks: the French built Fort Ouiatenon in 1717, with French settlement on the north bank and Wea villages on the south. In 1928, physician Richard B. Wetherill acquired land thought to be the fort site and built a replica there in 1930. Archaeologists confirmed the original location in the late 1960s, about a mile west of the park.

Take the stops in this order: Ross Hills Park on West 50 South, Fort Ouiatenon on South River Road, then Tecumseh Trails Park on North River Road. The last park stands across from the Indiana Veterans’ Home, with a shelter house and a view over the Wabash.

moments.title: Ross Hills County Park
moments.text: Ross Hills has trails and a deck overlook within a 168-acre park. Its setting belongs to a larger stretch of protected river habitat. The Wabash Bluffs Bicentennial Nature Trust project purchased 59 acres between Black Rock Nature Preserve and Ross Hills, creating nearly four contiguous miles of habitat along the Wabash. That adjoining project includes bluffs 100 feet above the floodplain, a silt-stone barren ravine and oak woodland.
moments.notice: Ross Hills’ trails include a deck overlook.

moments.title: Fort Ouiatenon Historic Park
moments.text: The French trading post established in 1717 stood on the Wabash, with French settlement on the north bank and Wea villages on the south. The blockhouse at Fort Ouiatenon Historic Park dates to 1930, when physician Richard B. Wetherill built a replica on land thought to hold the French fort. The original site was confirmed archaeologically in the late 1960s, about a mile west. The replica also differs in construction: its horizontal logs follow a British blockhouse pattern, while the French fort used vertical logs. The county owns and maintains the park; the Tippecanoe County Historical Association programs the Blockhouse Museum.
moments.notice: The replica blockhouse uses horizontal logs; the original French fort used vertical logs.

moments.title: Tecumseh Trails Park
moments.text: Tecumseh Trails Park occupies 23 acres on North River Road, across from the Indiana Veterans’ Home. The park overlooks the Wabash River and has picnic areas and a shelter house.
moments.notice: The park overlooks the Wabash River.
